body:
Maybe related to this:
https://github.com/trpc/trpc/pull/5017

This is kinda worrying to be honest, second regression I have found without any major version changes.
Love this library, but wondering how can I have confidence in updating versions if stuff may just break with a minor version change?

In our projects we always run "npm update" before we deploy stuff so this just breaks without any warning causing us the need to pin versions, which I want to avoid. 
Again thanks a lot for your hard work!

I'm sorry you're experiencing issues with the newest patch version and would definitely like to help, but I would really need some kind of way to reproduce your problem.

EDIT: I think I can reproduce it using your code sample

@omridevk :

What is the type of `...(opts.ctx as Context<Partial<CreateFastifyContextOptions>>),` in your app? What about `auth`?

EDIT 1:

I'm a bit worried about the amount of type assertions (`as`) you are using in your code. E.g. `makeTRPC` constructs `t` using a generic but then the middleware does this `...(opts.ctx as Simplify<
              Context<Partial<CreateFastifyContextOptions>>
            >` thing. At least it's making it very hard to know what's actually going on, sorry. The tRPC types are very complex.
            
EDIT 2:

If I take away the generic from your `makeTRPC` and replace the construction of `t` with `const t = initTRPC.context<Context<CreateFastifyContextOptions>>()` the error goes away. So this has something to do with `makeTRPC` in your application accepting an arbitrary type parameter. I'm still unsure why the change to `Overwrite` made it start failing though, although it's clear that it did. Is there a way for you to restructure your code to use less type assertions and have `makeTRPC` not take a type argument? Just asking.

Either way it would help to know what your context type is in your actual app.
not sure how I can make `makeTRPC` non generic, how will I type the context when using the makeTRPC?

the idea was that I can do something like this:
``` const {router} = makeTRPC<{myContext: string}>() ```

we have a lot of microservices, every service can have different context.
And really appreciate your help, thanks a lot :)
This also makes the error go away for me: `makeTRPC<TFoo extends CreateFastifyContextOptions>`
`TFoo extends object` also works

This would explain the error as well. `Overwrite` was changed to only overwrite keys of objects, and `T` with no object constraint works differently now. 

Still can't 100% explain to you the behavior, but if you can work with `makeTRPC` accepting a type argument with the `object` constraint I think this solves your immediate problem.
same error when changing to extend object
Ok, at this point I'm just going to need a better reproduction then :( since using your code sample the error goes away for me if I constrain `T` to `object`, sorry.
no problem, let me try to create a stackblitz. thanks for the help

@jussisaurio  can you share your code that you were able to get it work?

So I think the big pain is with typescript here, t.middleware has never been particularly good because Typescript has problems inferring its inputs/outputs properly in the chain. Partly this is related to the complexity of the types which v11 is going to dramatically improve. Lots of efforts to make this better but having done a 1000 line test file and project around this earlier in the year and abandoning it I suggest a different pattern for this type of thing https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-nqqlsq-shycwu?file=src%2Fserver%2Fmake-trpc.ts

Thanks for the stackblitz @omridevk .

I think we probably need to roll back [these changes](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/pull/5017) and replace them with an equivalent implementation that doesn't touch Overwrite.

The trouble is that tRPC types are complex enough that the only way to be able to make changes to internal types with confidence is to keep extending the regression test set.
@omridevk I rolled back the changes from #5017 (locally) and your stackblitz repro example still fails to compile for some reason :/

@jussisaurio I can try and make a minimal repro a bit later.

I managed to repro this now. @sentry/node (whose trpc middleware you are using) is also constructing trpc middlewares using an unconstrained type parameter `T` which I think is something that both of your problems share. I'll post a PR with reproing test soon

EDIT: @JoeKarow I arrived at this conclusion because I think you're experiencing errors with extending your `baseProcedure` which uses the Sentry middleware, but doing e.g. `t.procedure.use(isAuthed)` works fine.

Ah, yeah - it is the Sentry middleware that is causing it.. it looks like they're doing some changes on their end too. https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-javascript/issues/9536

To be clear, it's the change in tRPC that is causing it. It is just manifesting when using the sentry middleware. For example @omridevk is not using Sentry and experiencing a similar issue. Hopefully the linked PR resolves both.

Extending `ProcedureBuilder<any>` doesn't do what you want here; it basically infers all the procedure params as `any` instead of narrowing.
@omridevk I've added the example you gave as a new test to our test set (see link above), let me know if that implementation works for you

> @omridevk try:
> 
> ```
> import { ProcedureBuilder, ProcedureParams } from '@trpc/server';
> 
> ...
> 
> function withAuth2<T extends ProcedureParams>(builder: ProcedureBuilder<T>) {
> ```

Great point, that does fix it! Though I couldn't explain why that works. `extends X` should just mean 'any type which is at least this and puts anything in place of `any`' but that so often seems not to behave with our types 😳
Yeah I couldn't tell you why exactly that happens here. 🤷‍♂️
Closing this, feel free to ask to reopen if the problem still persists; the solution above (or the alternative by Nick) should work
